703209.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gʷənā. Cognates include the first element in Mycenaean Greek 𐀓𐀙𐀊 (ku-na-ja), Sanskrit ग्ना (gnā́), जनि॑ (jáni), Old Armenian կին (kin), and Old English cwēn (English queen).

703202.t: From Proto-Hellenic *gumnós (with Cowgill's Law: o → u between labial and resonant), from Proto-Indo-European *nogʷnós by metathesis (possible taboo deformation; if the metathesis didn't happen we would have *νυγνός (*nugnós)), from *nogʷós (“naked”).

703270.t: Thematicization of δάμνημι (dámnēmi, “to subdue”). Cognates include Sanskrit दाम्यति (dāmyati), Latin domō.

703255.t: From Proto-Indo-European *dáḱru. Cognates include Latin lacruma, Gothic 𐍄𐌰𐌲𐍂 (tagr), Old English tēar, Sanskrit अश्रु॑ (áśru) and Old Armenian արտաւսր (artawsr).

703250.t: From δαίομαι (daíomai, “to divide”) + -μων (-mōn), from Proto-Indo-European *deh₂y- (“to share, to divide”), thus literally “divider”, “allotter”.

703226.t: Inherited from Proto-Hellenic *gonwía, from *gónu (“knee”, whence γόνυ (gónu)), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *ǵónu (“id”).

703210.t: From Proto-Indo-European *gew- (“to curve, to bend”), the same source as Old Armenian կոր (kor), Lithuanian gur̃nas (“ankle, hip, bone”), and Norwegian kaure (“curly lock of hair”). See also γυῖον (guîon, “hand; limbs”).

703259.t: Uncertain; probably Pre-Greek. Possibly related to Latin digitus, though the details are unclear.

703287.t: From δάπτω (dáptō, “to devour, consume”) + -άνη (-ắnē). Compare semantically Latin damnum (“fine, mulct, penalty”).

703280.t: From δανείζω (dăneízō, “to lend money”) + -τής (-tḗs, masculine agentive suffix).

703249.t: Neuter gender of δαιμόνιος (daimónĭos, “extraordinary, divine; pertaining to daimones”).

703299.t: Probably from Proto-Indo-European *dn̥s-, zero-grade of *dens- (“thick, dense”), and cognate with Latin dēnsus (“dense”), Hittite [script needed] (daššu-, “heavy, strong”), though this depends on whether *-n̥s- does yield *-σ- (*-s-) in Greek.

703201.t: From the stem of γυμνάζω (gumnázō, “to exercise”), from γυμνός (gumnós, “naked”), and -ιον (-ion), neuter of adjective suffix -ιος (-ios).

703254.t: From Proto-Indo-European *denḱ- (“to bite”). Cognate with Sanskrit दशति (daśati, “to bite”), Old English ġetingan (“to press upon”), and Albanian darë.

703271.t: From Proto-Indo-European *demh₂- (“to domesticate, tame”) with the same *-l- suffix as found in δαμάλης (damálēs).
